content:
Luxembourg is Europe's quiet overperformer for doctoral pay: the University of Luxembourg hires PhD researchers as employees at roughly €44,531 per year (about €3,710/month gross) according to current listings — more than German or Dutch doctoral contracts at entry level. Add a trilingual environment, strong AI and security research groups, and a small-but-dense funding ecosystem, and Luxembourg deserves a place on every funded-PhD shortlist.

What PhD researchers in Luxembourg are paid

Funding sourceTypical payStructure
University of Luxembourg doctoral contract≈€44,531/year gross (≈€3,710/month)Full employment: pension, health, 25+ leave days
FNR PRIDE doctoral unitsComparable salaried contractsNational Research Fund structured programmes
FNR Industrial PhD (with a company)Employment contract + industrial top-upSplit between university and company
MSCA Doctoral Network positions≈€3,400/month gross (adjusted)EU-funded network positions hosted in Luxembourg

Unlike a stipend, the salary is taxable and social charges apply — but it also means pension contributions, full health coverage and unemployment insurance from day one. Net pay for a single researcher is typically around €2,800–3,000/month.

[[chart:lux-pay]]

Live doctoral positions in Luxembourg

Current listings on NextApply include positions across engineering, chemistry, AI, cybersecurity and business:

PositionGroup / focus
Doctoral researcher — Agentic AI, Digital Business & Information SystemsAI, information systems
Doctoral researcher — AI CybersecuritySecurity, machine learning
Doctoral researcher — Network Traffic ObfuscationNetworking, privacy
Doctoral researcher — AI4TEC Environmental ChemistryEnvironmental sciences + AI
Doctoral researcher — Water Engineering / PFAS monitoringEnvironmental engineering

University positions are posted on the university's careers portal and usually stay open until filled — apply early rather than waiting for a deadline.

Cost of living: the honest numbers

  • Housing is the big one: a studio in Luxembourg City commonly runs €900–1,400/month; living just across the border in France, Belgium or Germany and commuting can cut that by a third (cross-border workers get a tax adjustment instead of the standard deduction).
  • Food and transport: groceries are close to German prices; public transport is free nationwide — a real salary multiplier.
  • Net effect: on a €44,531 contract, single researchers in the city typically save €500–900/month; cross-border arrangements save more.

How to apply

  1. Find the group first: Luxembourg's research is concentrated — the university's SnT (security/ICT), LCSB (systems biomedicine) and FSTM (science/technology) host most doctoral positions.
  2. Apply to the vacancy with a CV, transcripts, two references and a short statement; shortlisting usually takes 3–6 weeks.
  3. Formal doctoral enrolment follows the job offer — you apply to the doctoral school after being hired, not before.
  4. English is the working language; IELTS is listed on some positions but English-taught degrees are widely accepted — see our guide to studying in Europe without IELTS.

Luxembourg vs the neighbours

CountryEntry doctoral pay (approx.)Net (single, approx.)
Luxembourg€44,531/year€2,800–3,000/month

United Kingdom£21,805/year stipend (tax-free)£1,817/month

Questions applicants often ask

Do I need French, German or Luxembourgish? No — doctoral work is in English; administrative life runs happily on English too.

Is the degree respected internationally? Yes — the University of Luxembourg ranks among the world's top young universities, and its CS/security groups publish at top venues.

Family relocation? Salaried contracts support family reunification visas; see our PhD dependant visa comparison.

The research groups worth knowing

  • SnT — Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust: Luxembourg's largest ICT research centre; cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, AI verification, space systems. Hosts most of the university's AI-security doctoral positions.
  • LCSB — Luxembourg Centre for Systems Biomedicine: neuroscience, Parkinson's disease, digital health cohorts; strong computational biology.
  • FSTM — Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine: engineering, physics, materials; hosts the water/PFAS and environmental AI positions.
  • Department of Finance and Management: the digital business and agentic-AI doctoral projects sit here.

Application timeline reality check

StageTypical duration
Vacancy posted → your applicationApply within 2–3 weeks of posting (rolling review)
Shortlisting3–6 weeks
Interview + decision2–4 weeks (often 2 remote rounds)
Contract + enrolment3–4 weeks
Residence permit (non-EU)4–10 weeks (start immediately after contract)

Total: plan 3–5 months from application to arrival. Since most Luxembourg positions are rolling, the bottleneck is usually the permit for non-EU applicants — see our family visa comparison if relocating with dependants.

Questions applicants often ask (continued)

Can I do a part-time doctorate? Rare on university contracts; FNR-funded positions are full-time by design.

Is a master's required? For most doctoral contracts yes, or a bachelor's with research experience — see PhD without a master's for country rules.
